slides.say: Three circles with centers A, B and C touch one another from the outside. Their radii are six centimeters, fourteen centimeters and fifteen centimeters. What is the length of the highlighted arc of the circle with center A, in centimeters?
We need the length of an arc. An arc is part of the circumference. Its length is the angle out of three hundred sixty, times two pi r, the whole circumference.
at: We need the length of an arc

slides.say: [short pause] The radius of circle A is given, so the whole circumference is easy. Two pi r is two pi times six, which is twelve pi.
at: Two pi r is two pi times six

slides.say: Let's peek at the choices. Choice number one is twelve pi. That's the whole circle, and the highlighted arc is only part of it, so it has to be less. Choice number one is out.

We can also cross out choice number four, six pi. Six pi is exactly half the circle. Let's connect the three centers. The highlighted arc's angle at A is three hundred sixty minus the triangle's angle at A. For the arc to be exactly half, that triangle angle would have to be one hundred eighty. But an angle of a triangle is always less than one hundred eighty. So the highlighted arc is more than half, and choice number four is out too.
at: would have to be one hundred eighty
and choice number four is out too

slides.say: To choose between choice number two and choice number three, let's find the angle. If you're ever out of time at this point, guess one of the two. That's a one in two chance instead of one in four.

[short pause] Here are the three circles again, bigger. Let's put in the givens. The radius of circle A is six, so we write six and six on its two radii. Circle B, fourteen and fourteen. Circle C, fifteen and fifteen.
at: Here are the three circles again

slides.say: The circles touch, so the line between two centers passes through the point where they touch. It's made of the two radii. So A B is six plus fourteen, twenty. A C is six plus fifteen, twenty-one. And B C is fourteen plus fifteen, twenty-nine.
at: So A B is six plus fourteen
A C is six plus fifteen
And B C is fourteen plus

slides.say: Twenty, twenty-one, twenty-nine. We need the angle at A, so let's check Pythagoras, to see if it's a right angle. Twenty squared is four hundred. Twenty-one squared is four hundred forty-one. Together, eight hundred forty-one.

And twenty-nine squared? It's twenty-nine times thirty, minus twenty-nine. Twenty-nine times thirty is eight hundred seventy. Eight hundred seventy minus twenty-nine is eight hundred forty-one. The same, so it's a Pythagorean triple.
B C, twenty-nine, is the hypotenuse, so the angle across from it, the angle at A, is ninety degrees.
at: the angle at A, is ninety

slides.say: [short pause] Now let's look only at circle A. The angle at A is ninety degrees. So the arc we don't need, inside that angle, is ninety out of three hundred sixty. That's a quarter of the circle.
at: Now let's look only at circle A
So the arc we don't need
That's a quarter of the circle

slides.say: And the highlighted arc is the rest, three quarters of the circumference.
at: the highlighted arc is the rest

slides.say: Three quarters of twelve pi. Let's find a quarter first. Twelve pi divided by four is three pi. So three quarters is three times three pi, which is nine pi. Choice number three is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
